notes: Covers the main email-plus-wildcard case, but it always creates a policy (true is passed unconditionally), so output differs from the dummy-site-block equivalent when no global ACME options are set. Internal-only names get a policy with no issuers instead of the internal issuer, so they fall back to ACME when there is no http app. Subjects are also re-sorted, which changes the adapt output and likely explains the hidden test failure.

It always creates an issuerless policy (base policy built with always=true), even without global options, which breaks parity with a dummy site block; it splits off an internal issuer only when public and internal names are mixed, so a list of only `localhost`/IPs gets no internal issuer; tests are thorough but miss these cases, and the hidden test fails.

The production code matches the reference: append-on-repeat parsing, an existing site policy wins, non-public names go to internalAP, and a policy is only created when global ACME defaults exist (shared helper factored out). Thorough unit and adapt tests cover the spec's cases.

Implementation matches the reference: names are appended to the automate loader, non-public names go to the internal policy, existing site-block policies are respected, and a global-defaults policy is created only when needed; unit tests and caddyfiletest fixtures cover wildcard, no-site, repeated, internal, HTTP-only, existing-policy and auto_https off cases.
